question:
An 20-year-old female college student with a history of sickle cell anemia reports experiencing one to
two painful crises annually that require hospitalization. She has no history of red-cell transfusions. She

experiences intermittent pain in her extremities and midback, which is managed with nonsteroidal
anti-inflammatory drugs or acetaminophen-hydrocodone. The patient recalls episodes of confusion,
slurred speech, and weakness in her left arm and leg that resolved within minutes. The first episode
occurred in her early teens, and she attributed it to sleep deprivation. A similar episode happened last
year while studying for final exams, which she also attributed to lack of sleep. Her regular medication is
norethindrone. She occasionally experiences migraines around her menstrual periods. She does not
smoke or use illicit drugs but drinks alcohol occasionally. Which of the following is the most appropriate
first-line treatment for stroke prevention in this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Clopidogrel (B) Voxelotor
(C) Aspirin (D) Red-cell exchange transfusions (E) Combination antiplatelet therapy (F) Regular
phlebotomy (G) Chronic simple transfusions (H) Prophylactic anticoagulation (I) L-glutamine
supplementation (J) Hydroxyurea
 A. Regular phlebotomy
B. Clopidogrel
C. Red-cell exchange transfusions
D. Voxelotor
E. Combination antiplatelet therapy
F. L-glutamine supplementation
G. Prophylactic anticoagulation
H. Chronic simple transfusions
I. Hydroxyurea
J. Aspirin
